topic: Retrofit internals: proxies, converters & call adapters

questions.question: What does `retrofit.create(ApiService::class.java)` return?
options: A subclass of `ApiService` produced by R8 during the build
An instance of a class generated at compile time by an annotation processor
A wrapper around OkHttpClient that parses annotations on every request
A dynamic proxy implementing the interface, whose method calls go to Retrofit's invocation handler
questions.explanation: Retrofit uses `java.lang.reflect.Proxy` to create an implementation of your interface at runtime. Each method call goes to an `InvocationHandler`, which looks up or builds the parsed description of that method and runs it. There is no code generation step.

questions.question: Retrofit service declarations must be interfaces; passing an abstract class to `create()` fails.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: `java.lang.reflect.Proxy` can only implement interfaces, and Retrofit validates this up front, throwing an `IllegalArgumentException` for anything else. Interfaces that extend other interfaces are allowed.

questions.question: A Retrofit function is declared as `suspend fun getUser(id: String): User`. What happens when the server returns HTTP 404?
options: It throws an `HttpException`
It returns `null`
It returns a `User` with default field values
It suspends forever until a 2xx arrives
questions.explanation: When the return type is the body itself, a non-2xx response has no body to return, so Retrofit throws `HttpException`. Declare `Response<User>` instead if you want to inspect the status code without catching exceptions.

questions.question: A Retrofit builder adds the Gson converter factory first and the scalars converter factory second. An endpoint returns `String`. What happens?
options: Retrofit falls back to its built-in String converter
The scalars converter is used because it is more specific
Gson handles it because converters are tried in order and Gson accepts any type
Retrofit throws because two converters match
questions.explanation: Retrofit asks each converter factory in the order added and uses the first that returns a converter. The Gson factory accepts any type, so it tries to parse the body as a JSON string. Add the scalars factory before the JSON factory if you want raw strings.

questions.question: Why is the first call to each Retrofit endpoint a little slower, and how can you move that cost to `create()` time?
options: OkHttp opens a new connection for each method; setting a connection pool fixes it
Converters are instantiated lazily; adding them in a fixed order fixes it
The proxy class is regenerated on each first call; enabling R8 fixes it
Each method's annotations are parsed and cached on first use; `validateEagerly(true)` parses all methods when the service is created
questions.explanation: Retrofit parses a method's annotations, parameters, converters and call adapter into a cached object the first time it is invoked. `validateEagerly(true)` does that for all methods at `create()`, which also surfaces declaration errors early, at the cost of startup time.

questions.question: Which statements about Retrofit's built-in `suspend` support are true? Select all that apply.
options: A suspend function returning `Response<T>` does not throw for non-2xx status codes
Retrofit detects a suspend method by its compiler-added `Continuation` parameter
Retrofit switches the call to `Dispatchers.IO` before running it
It is safe to call from the main thread, since the request is executed asynchronously by OkHttp
It requires adding a coroutine call adapter factory
questions.explanation: At the bytecode level a suspend function has an extra `Continuation` parameter, which Retrofit uses to detect it. It enqueues the OkHttp call and resumes on completion, so the caller does not block. No extra adapter is needed, and it does not use `Dispatchers.IO`; the work runs on OkHttp's own threads.

questions.question: If the coroutine calling a Retrofit suspend function is cancelled while the request is in flight, Retrofit cancels the underlying OkHttp call.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Retrofit installs a cancellation handler that cancels the OkHttp `Call` when the coroutine is cancelled. That is why leaving a screen with `viewModelScope` cancels its pending requests instead of letting them finish in the background.

questions.question: You want `suspend fun getUser(): NetworkResult<User>` to never throw, with errors wrapped in `NetworkResult.Error`. How does a custom `CallAdapter.Factory` get involved?
options: Retrofit asks the factory for `Deferred<NetworkResult<User>>` and awaits it
Call adapters are skipped for suspend functions, so a converter must do the wrapping
Retrofit asks the factory for an adapter for `Call<NetworkResult<User>>`, so it must handle that wrapped type and return a Call that turns errors into values
Retrofit asks the factory for an adapter for `NetworkResult<User>`, and the adapter returns that value directly
questions.explanation: For suspend functions Retrofit treats the declared return type R as if the method returned `Call<R>`, looks up an adapter for that, then awaits the adapted Call. A wrapping adapter therefore matches `Call<NetworkResult<T>>` and returns a Call whose callback always succeeds with a success or error value. Converters only turn bytes into objects and cannot handle network failures.

questions.question: Which statements follow from Retrofit's runtime proxy design? Select all that apply.
options: A new proxy class is generated for every method call
Retrofit generates source files for the interface during kapt or KSP
Calling `toString()` on the service instance does not make an HTTP request
If R8 strips generic signatures, Retrofit can fail at runtime to resolve return types like `Response<User>`
questions.explanation: The invocation handler passes `Object` methods like `toString()` through without treating them as endpoints. Because Retrofit reads generic types by reflection at runtime, shrinking that removes signatures breaks it, which is why it ships keep rules. The proxy class is created once per interface, and there is no code generation.

questions.question: What URL path does this produce when called with `getFile("docs/readme.md")`?
questions.code:
@GET("files/{path}")
suspend fun getFile(@Path("path") path: String): ResponseBody
options: It throws, because `@Path` values cannot contain slashes
`files/docs/readme.md`
`files/` followed by the value in a query parameter
`files/docs%2Freadme.md`
questions.explanation: `@Path` values are URL-encoded by default, so the slash becomes `%2F` and the value stays one path segment. Use `@Path("path", encoded = true)` when you intentionally want to insert multiple segments. This default protects against callers injecting extra path segments.
